question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

-24, -95, -379, -1515, ?, -24235
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. -6059.

GIVEN

• -24, -95, -379, -1515, ?, -24235

SOLUTION

• Each term follows the rule (previous term × 4) + 1.

• -24 × 4 + 1 = -95; -95 × 4 + 1 = -379; -379 × 4 + 1 = -1515.

• Missing term = -1515 × 4 + 1 = -6060 + 1 = -6059.

• Check: -6059 × 4 + 1 = -24236 + 1 = -24235. ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• When terms grow ~4×, test the rule ×4±1. Here ×4 then +1 fits every step.

NOTE

• For fast-growing series, always check multiply-then-add/subtract patterns (×n±k) before differences.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

V, U, R, M, ?, W, L, Y
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. F.

GIVEN

• V, U, R, M, ?, W, L, Y

SOLUTION

• Positions (A=1…Z=26): V=22, U=21, R=18, M=13.

• Differences are consecutive odd numbers: -1, -3, -5, -7, -9, -11, -13 (wrap around 26).

• 22-1=21(U); 21-3=18(R); 18-5=13(M); 13-7=6=F.

• Continue: 6-9=-3→23(W); 23-11=12(L); 12-13=-1→25(Y). ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract 1,3,5,7… in turn; M(13) minus 7 = 6 = F.

NOTE

• Odd-difference letter series (-1,-3,-5…) are common in SSC; use position numbers and wrap past A/Z.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter cluster in the same way as the fourth letter cluster is related to the third letter cluster and sixth letter cluster is related to fifth letter cluster.

OTF : ? :: HAC : JCE :: GVB : IXD
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. QVH.

GIVEN

• OTF : ? :: HAC : JCE :: GVB : IXD

SOLUTION

• Rule (from the known pairs): add +2 to every letter.

• HAC → J,C,E (H+2, A+2, C+2) = JCE. ✓  GVB → I,X,D (G+2, V+2, B+2) = IXD. ✓

• So OTF → O+2=Q, T+2=V, F+2=H = QVH.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Same +2 shift on each letter: O→Q, T→V, F→H = QVH.

NOTE

• In analogy clusters, find the constant letter-shift from any solved pair and apply it to the target.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

FPG : JTK :: ? : NXZ :: RYE : VCI
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. JTV.

GIVEN

• FPG : JTK :: ? : NXZ :: RYE : VCI

SOLUTION

• Rule: add +4 to every letter. FPG → J,T,K = JTK. ✓  RYE → V,C,I = VCI. ✓

• The unknown cluster gives NXZ on +4, so unknown = NXZ − 4: N-4=J, X-4=T, Z-4=V = JTV.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Since target+4 = NXZ, just subtract 4: N→J, X→T, Z→V = JTV.

NOTE

• When the result is given but the base is asked, reverse the shift (subtract instead of add).

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

AZ, YU, WP, UK, SF, QA, ?, MQ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. OV.

GIVEN

• AZ, YU, WP, UK, SF, QA, ?, MQ

SOLUTION

• First letters: A, Y, W, U, S, Q, ?, M → decreasing by 2 (wrap): A→Y→W→U→S→Q→O→M.

• Second letters: Z, U, P, K, F, A, ?, Q → decreasing by 5 (wrap): F→A→(A-5=V)→(V-5=Q). ✓

• Missing term = OV.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Handle the two letters separately: 1st -2, 2nd -5. From QA: Q-2=O, A-5=V → OV.

NOTE

• Split two-letter series into two independent single-letter series; wrap A(1)↔Z(26).

question: What was the day of the week on 16 January 2003?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Thursday.

GIVEN

• Find the day on 16 January 2003.

SOLUTION

• Odd days up to 2000 = 0. Years 2001, 2002 (both ordinary) = 2 odd days → 31 Dec 2002 = Tuesday.

• So 1 Jan 2003 = Wednesday.

• From 1 Jan to 16 Jan = 15 extra days; 15 ÷ 7 remainder 1 → Wednesday + 1 = Thursday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• 1 Jan 2003 = Wednesday; 16th = 1st + 15 days = +1 weekday = Thursday.

NOTE

• Odd days: 0=Sun…6=Sat. 100 yrs=5, 200=3, 300=1, 400=0; ordinary year=1, leap=2 odd days.

question: What was the day of the week on 15 July 2012?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Sunday.

GIVEN

• Find the day on 15 July 2012.

SOLUTION

• Odd days up to 2000 = 0. Years 2001–2011 = 11 years with 2 leap years (2004, 2008) → 11+2 = 13 → remainder 6 → 31 Dec 2011 = Saturday.

• So 1 Jan 2012 = Sunday. 2012 is a leap year.

• Days Jan 1 → July 15 = 31+29+31+30+31+30+15 = 197; days after Jan 1 = 196; 196 ÷ 7 = 0 remainder.

• So 15 July = same weekday as 1 Jan = Sunday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 1 Jan 2012 = Sunday; up to 15 July exactly 196 days (÷7) → same day = Sunday.

NOTE

• Remember Feb has 29 days in leap year 2012; count elapsed days from 1 Jan and take mod 7.

question: What was the last day of the year 1857?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Thursday.

GIVEN

• Find the day on 31 December 1857 (last day of 1857).

SOLUTION

• Odd days for complete years up to 1857:

• 1600 years → 0; next 200 years (1601–1800) → 3 odd days.

• 1801–1857 = 57 years with 14 leap years → 57+14 = 71 → 71 ÷ 7 remainder 1.

• Total = 0 + 3 + 1 = 4 odd days = Thursday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Odd days = 3 (for 1800) + (57 + 14) = 3 + 71 → 3 + 1 = 4 → Thursday.

NOTE

• Last day of a year = 31 Dec; use complete-year odd days. 4 odd days = Thursday (0=Sun).

question: 5 boys J, R, M, B and C are sitting in a row facing south (not necessarily in the same order). R is to the immediate right of M. B is to the immediate left of M. J is to the right of R. C is to the left of M. Who is at the right end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. J.

GIVEN

• 5 boys J, R, M, B, C in a row facing south.

• R immediate right of M; B immediate left of M; J right of R; C left of M.

SOLUTION

• Facing south, a person's right = West side, left = East side. Arrange West→East.

• R right of M → R M. B left of M → R M B. J right of R → J R M B. C left of M → placed to the East: J R M B C.

• Row West→East: J, R, M, B, C. The right end (West end) is J.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Facing south flips left/right; the person farthest to the observer's West is at the right end = J.

NOTE

• Facing South: your right = West, left = East (opposite of facing North). Always fix direction first.

question: 7 teachers A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). B is fifth to the left of E. A is fifth to the left of G. D is third to the left of E. C is second to the right of D. How many teachers are sitting between D and G?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• 7 teachers in a row facing north. B fifth-left of E; A fifth-left of G; D third-left of E; C second-right of D.

SOLUTION

• Number seats 1–7 (left→right). B = E−5 and D = E−3 → take E = 6, then B = 1, D = 3.

• C = D + 2 = 5. A = G − 5 → take G = 7, A = 2. Remaining seat 4 = F.

• Arrangement: 1-B, 2-A, 3-D, 4-F, 5-C, 6-E, 7-G.

• Between D(3) and G(7): seats 4, 5, 6 = F, C, E → 3 teachers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix E at seat 6 (as B needs 5 to its left); everything else falls into place, leaving 3 seats between D and G.

NOTE

• 'X is nth to the left of Y' → seat(X) = seat(Y) − n. Convert clues to seat numbers and place.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

GIVEN

• First pair: box (→, P / C, 6) is related to box (Ɔ, ← / ∂, q).

• Third box: (Δ, D / B, J). Find its matching figure.

SOLUTION

• The second figure is the mirror image (lateral inversion) of the first: every element is flipped left-to-right (→ becomes ←, 6 becomes its reverse, etc.).

• Apply the same mirror to (Δ, D / B, J): each letter is reversed and the columns swap, giving the reversed-letter box shown in Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Just take the mirror (left-right flip) of the third box; only Option 1 shows all four characters correctly reversed (note the reversed J).

NOTE

• Mirror image = left-right flip: characters reverse and left/right positions swap; water image = top-bottom flip. Read the arrow (→→←) to decide the rule.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

GIVEN

• First pair: a square is related to the same square with arrows drawn from the centre to each of its sides/corners.

• Third figure: a triangle. Find its matching figure.

SOLUTION

• Rule: add an arrow from the centre pointing to every vertex of the figure. A square (4 corners) gets 4 arrows.

• A triangle has 3 vertices, so it must get 3 arrows (to the top, bottom-left and bottom-right vertices).

• Only Option shows the triangle with arrows to all three vertices.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Count the corners of the base shape and match the same number of centre-to-corner arrows; triangle → 3 arrows = Option 4.

NOTE

• In figure analogies, first identify what is 'added' (here: arrows to each vertex), then apply it consistently to the new shape.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

MM167 : LP67 :: LL197 : KO97 :: NN207 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. MQ107.

GIVEN

• MM167 : LP67 :: LL197 : KO97 :: NN207 : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: 1st letter −1, 2nd letter +3, number −100.

• MM167 → M-1=L, M+3=P, 167-100=67 = LP67. ✓  LL197 → K, O, 97 = KO97. ✓

• NN207 → N-1=M, N+3=Q, 207-100=107 = MQ107.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply −1, +3 to the two letters and −100 to the number: N→M, N→Q, 207→107 = MQ107.

NOTE

• Treat the number as a whole (do not split digits). Find the fixed letter shifts and number operation from a solved pair.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. question:

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

5067 : ? :: 8425 : 8462 :: 6552 : 6589

The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 5104.

• 5067 : ? :: 8425 : 8462 :: 6552 : 6589

SOLUTION

• 8425 + 37 = 8462. ✓  6552 + 37 = 6589. ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

question:
Select the option that is related to the second number in the same way as the third number is related to the fourth number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

? : 230 :: 705 : 1406 :: 582 : 1160
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 117.

GIVEN

• ? : 230 :: 705 : 1406 :: 582 : 1160

SOLUTION

• Rule: first number × 2 − 4 = second number.

• 705 × 2 − 4 = 1410 − 4 = 1406. ✓  582 × 2 − 4 = 1164 − 4 = 1160. ✓

• So ? × 2 − 4 = 230 → ? × 2 = 234 → ? = 117.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the rule: (230 + 4) ÷ 2 = 234 ÷ 2 = 117.

NOTE

• When the result is given, reverse the operation: add back 4, then halve.

question: In a certain code language, 'uniform civil code formed' is coded as 'ps pm tq lz' and 'goa come under this code' is coded as 'pz tq lm zp ab'. How will 'code' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. tq.

GIVEN

• 'uniform civil code formed' = 'ps pm tq lz'

• 'goa come under this code' = 'pz tq lm zp ab'

SOLUTION

• The word common to both sentences is 'code'.

• The code common to both coded strings is 'tq'.

• Hence 'code' = tq.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Spot the shared word (code) and the shared code-token (tq) across the two lines.

NOTE

• In word-substitution coding, the common word maps to the common code between the two given sentences.

question: In a certain coded language 'SCOPE' is coded as 'TGMMZ' and 'PHASE' is coded as 'QLYPZ'. How will 'BONED' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. CSLBY.

GIVEN

• SCOPE → TGMMZ, PHASE → QLYPZ. Find code for BONED.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shift: +1, +4, −2, −3, −5.

• Check PHASE: P+1=Q, H+4=L, A−2=Y, S−3=P, E−5=Z = QLYPZ. ✓

• BONED → B+1=C, O+4=S, N−2=L, E−3=B, D−5=Y = CSLBY.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply the fixed shift pattern +1,+4,−2,−3,−5 to B,O,N,E,D → C,S,L,B,Y.

NOTE

• Derive the per-position shift from one known pair, verify with the second, then apply. Wrap A↔Z as needed.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

KT910, OO824, QJ738, TE652, WZ566, ZU480
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. OO824.

GIVEN

• KT910, OO824, QJ738, TE652, WZ566, ZU480

SOLUTION

• First letters should increase by +3: K, N, Q, T, W, Z.

• Second letters decrease by 5 (wrap): T, O, J, E, Z, U — all correct. Numbers decrease by 86: 910, 824, 738, 652, 566, 480 — all correct.

• Only the 2nd term is off: its first letter is O but should be N (K→N→Q…). So the wrong term is OO824 (should be NO824).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Check first letters K,?,Q,T,W,Z (+3 each) → the 2nd must be N, not O; the O-term is wrong.

NOTE

• In find-the-wrong-term, verify each component (1st letter, 2nd letter, number) as its own pattern.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

ZBU500, VGA502, RLG504, MQN505, JVS508, FAY510
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. MQN505.

GIVEN

• ZBU500, VGA502, RLG504, MQN505, JVS508, FAY510

SOLUTION

• Numbers should increase by +2 each: 500, 502, 504, 506, 508, 510.

• The 4th term has 505 instead of 506; also its 1st letter should be N (Z,V,R,N,J,F) not M and 3rd letter M not N.

• Hence the wrong term is MQN505 (correct would be NQM506).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• The numbers run 500,502,504,506,508,510 (+2); 505 breaks the pattern → MQN505 is wrong.

NOTE

• Numbers are often the quickest check; here +2 arithmetic immediately exposes the odd term.
